To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IBR techniques can use a diverse range of image- and geometry-based representations and that compression of such representations is an important research area.
IBR techniques can use images and geometry in diverse ways, and that compression techniques are important for making IBR techniques practically useful.

(1) the use of images in IBR techniques is more important than the use of geometry, (2) the use of geometry in IBR techniques can help improve rendering quality and reduce memory requirements, and (3) compression techniques specifically designed to exploit the characteristics of image-based representations can significantly reduce memory requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How much geometry is required in image-based representations?
the fundamental questions of what is the best way of representing a scene, how to compress such representations, and how to render novel views from such representations.
the fundamental problem of representing and compressing 3-D scene information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IBR techniques are a very diverse and active research field.
IBR techniques have been developed in a wide variety of ways.
the field of IBR has made great progress in the last 15 years, and it has matured to the stage that it is now ready for commercialization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IBR and compression techniques are two sides of the same coin.

IBR and compression techniques for image-based representations are complementary and that they can be combined in various ways to achieve different tradeoffs in the extent of use of geometry and in compression efficiency.
IBR techniques are not just a new way of rendering, but also a new way of representing 3-D objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single best IBR technique for all applications.
there are many ways to represent 3-D scenes using images and geometry.
IBR techniques are not only a set of rendering techniques but also a set of image-based representations, and the two are closely related.
